Swiss Army Bench 0.0.12: Launch Claude, data and app notebooks, and the app's name in the corner.

- **Launch Claude** (the footer, with our own sparkle): opens Claude Code in your terminal, in a folder made for
  it: a CLAUDE.md about Swiss Army Bench and what you have open (table names, columns and steps; never your
  rows), the app's tools connected, and your project's files. Or opens Claude Desktop with the app's tools added
  to its settings (it asks once, keeps everything else, and makes a backup first).
- **Finds Claude wherever it is installed**, including company-managed installs: the registry, Store packages and
  Start menu on Windows; the Applications folders and Spotlight on macOS; launcher entries on Linux. Settings'
  Claude section shows what was found, lets you pick another, and has a switch to start Claude Code with its
  permission prompts skipped (off unless you turn it on; only you can change it). Not installed: how to install it.
- **Data and app notebooks:** in a project, data.ipynb is the data notebook and every other notebook is an app
  notebook, each with its own icon and word. The Notebooks page groups them; New makes an app notebook. The Data
  panel shows beside app notebooks and apps, not beside the data notebook.
- **The app's name and version** at the bottom left of every status bar.
- **Check for updates** in Settings is a button: it checks now and starts the update when there is one. The
  automatic check keeps its switch ("Check every six hours").

Update from the tray (right-click, Update to 0.0.12), or:

```powershell
irm https://github.com/DylanCodyBrown/SwissArmyBench/releases/latest/download/install.ps1 | iex
```
